notes.text: Available in cPanel & WHM 11 and later, according to the pinned operation. Replaces the reseller privilege set. Read current privileges first and construct the complete desired replacement. Use either a named acllist, which replaces the assigned set from that list, or inline acl-* switches, never both. In inline mode each true sends the key with value 1; null or omission excludes that privilege from the replacement. With no named list and no inline switches, all privileges are removed. false and integer values are rejected before dispatch because upstream grants any supplied acl-* key regardless of its value. acl-all grants root-level privileges. Preserve assignment-only acl-disallow-shell and acl-nameserver-config wire names. The source recommends managing ACLs through WHM.

The backward-compatible user alias overrides reseller in reviewed upstream source, so it is omitted from this typed signature. The required reseller argument is the sole typed account selector; the alias remains reachable through generic call(). No alias-resolution rule is inferred beyond the reviewed source.

The pinned acl-disallow-shell description says to allow shell-account creation, contradicting the wire name. Its shell-access meaning remains unresolved; the client preserves the exact assignment key without asserting either interpretation. All assignment behavior here is source-backed and tested offline; no reseller write was observed.
